# BamDude

> Self-hosted print archive, farm management and automation for Bambu Lab 3D printers. It runs on your own hardware and talks to the printers over the local network, with no Bambu Cloud account required. Free and open source (AGPL-3.0), in English and Ukrainian.

BamDude (in Cyrillic, БамДуд) connects to Bambu Lab printers over local MQTT and file transfer with Developer Mode enabled. It works for one printer and for a whole print farm: every print is archived with its 3MF, work is queued per printer or routed automatically to a compatible one, and a full Telegram bot controls the farm from a phone. It is a hard fork of Bambuddy, developed independently; a Bambuddy installation can be migrated.

Supported printers: X1 (X1, X1C, X1E), H2 (H2D, H2D Pro, H2C, H2S), P1 (P1P, P1S), P2 (P2S), A1 (A1, A1 mini), A2 (A2L) and X2 (X2D).

## What it does

- Monitoring and control: live printer status, a multi-printer dashboard, camera streaming and a camera wall, temperatures, fans and motion control, AMS management, HMS error decoding, the printer's file browser, LAN firmware updates, and a mobile PWA.
- Print farm queue: a queue per printer with parallel background dispatch, Auto-Queue routing to a printer whose model, filament and feeds match the job, rebalancing across printer models, staggered start, swap mode for A1 plate swappers, preheat and heat soak, and G-code macros.
- Print archive: every print kept with its source 3MF and metadata, a 3D viewer, full-text search, photos and notes, a timelapse editor, failure analysis, and CSV / XLSX export.
- File library: uploads and folders, a gallery per plate, STL and STEP thumbnails, MakerWorld import, a Manyfold library as a model source, project assembly from several models, and server-side slicing through an OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio sidecar.
- Orders and products: orders list what was asked for, products say which parts they are made of, the print plan for each order line, stock of finished goods and spare parts, and defects counted against the order.
- Spools and filament: a built-in spool inventory or two-way Spoolman sync, automatic consumption tracking per print, a filament ledger, spool labels with QR codes, stock forecasting, and filament families as the slicers model them.
- Filament calibration: Pressure Advance, flow rate and temperature / speed / retraction towers, sliced against your own presets; K-profiles kept per printer, filament, nozzle and extruder.
- Maintenance: maintenance tasks for each printer model, hour and calendar counters with overdue alerts, maintenance mode, and archived printers.
- Automation: smart plugs (Zigbee without a separate bridge, Tasmota, Home Assistant, MQTT, REST), energy per print, environment sensors, a virtual printer so a slicer can send to the farm, and optional AI failure detection with Obico on your own server or OctoEverywhere's cloud.
- Telegram bot: printer control, the queue, printing from the library, calibration and maintenance from chat, several chats with their own roles.
- Notifications: an in-app inbox and 11 channels: Telegram, Discord, Email (SMTP), Pushover, ntfy, Bark, Gotify, CallMeBot, Signal, Home Assistant and webhooks.
- Access and integrations: granular permissions with Admin / Operator / Viewer groups, TOTP, email codes and backup codes, OIDC single sign-on, LDAP / Active Directory, API keys that can be limited to chosen printers, a REST and WebSocket API, Prometheus metrics, MQTT publishing, Git backup, a read-only MCP server for AI assistants (development preview) and an opt-in link to BamDude Cloud.
- Deployment: one Docker container (amd64 and arm64), a native Windows installer, or an install script for Linux and macOS. SQLite out of the box; PostgreSQL bundled or your own server.
